claim: Quoted DOT strings only handle the quote escape as Graphviz does, so the writer emits strings Graphviz cannot parse and the reader misreads an escaped backslash before a quote

triage.scenario: Take a page named `C:\` or a node id `ends\`. `dotId` and `quoteLabel` write it as `"C:\\"`. In Graphviz's lexer, `\"` is the only escape, so `\\"` reads as a literal backslash followed by an escaped quote. The string does not end at that quote and runs on to the next `"`, so Graphviz rejects the file or reads it wrongly. This package's own lexer reads `\\` as a pair (line 72) and accepts the file, which is why write.test.ts's "ids … holding backslashes" round trip passes. The same rule hurts on the read side. A Graphviz file whose string holds `\\"`, such as `label="a\\"b"` (which is `a\"b` to Graphviz), gets cut at that quote here. `nameOf` (parse.ts:54) also folds `\\` to `\` in ids, so the distinct Graphviz nodes `"a\\b"` and `"a\b"` merge into one node. Only `\"` should be special. A trailing backslash should be written so Graphviz reads it (for example, split with a line continuation) rather than as `\\"`.
triage.cause: the lexer treats `\\` as an escape that Graphviz does not have

exportPageOf climbs past the page run, so a follower kept in the run exports to whichever page the whole run's bounds favor

triage.scenario: a diagram cluster (its `dependsOn` names its members) whose members sit on two pages is placed in the page run (`placeOnPages`: "a node following others goes … else into the page run"). `documentFromScene` → `pageOf(cluster)` → `pageIdOf` is null (the run is not a page), so the loop climbs to the outermost ancestor, the page run node itself, and `documentBoundsOf(run)` spans every page; `pageHolding` then answers from the bounds of all pages, not from the cluster's own box, putting the cluster (and its `itemPage`) on an arbitrary page. It should stop below page structure (`isPageStructure`) and measure the node's own outermost non-structure ancestor.
triage.cause: ancestor walk does not stop at page structure

triage.scenario: a sequence diagram inside a group or container (`pageRootsOf` skips it, so its page stays a graph page), or a second sequence on a page: `kind === 'sequence'` hits `continue` without setting `bucket.sequence`, so the diagram is in no page and nothing reports it lost; the exported graph page has its group but not the sequence it held
triage.cause: non-root sequences neither exported nor reported

claim: documentFromScene drops a shape's header band and header text colors

triage.scenario: a class box (header row) whose `colors` set `header: '#ff0000'` and/or `headerText: '#00ff00'` is drawn by `diagramScene` (the band's paint goes on the node's `headerFill`, the title's on the header row's fill via `rowTextColor`, packages/diagram/src/dataColors.ts:42-54). `readShape` builds `colors` from `fill`, `stroke`, the first *non-header* row's text fill, `strokeWidth` and `dash` only; nothing in the package reads `headerFill` or a header row's fill (grep for `headerText|headerFill` in diagram-formats is empty). So the scene → document → JSON round trip (the native format, "which carries everything the model holds") comes back with the theme's header colors. Also, a node whose only text row is its header (a folded class box, or one with no fields) gets `text` from `dataOf(undefined)`, so an own text color is lost too and returns to the theme's when it is expanded.
triage.cause: reader omits NodeStyle fields `header`/`headerText`

claim: An empty bb attribute makes DOT pos read as points instead of inches

triage.scenario: `digraph { bb=""; a [pos="1,1"]; b [pos="2,1"] }`. `str(root.graph,'bb')` is `''`, which is not `undefined`, so `unit` is 1 and the positions are taken as points: a 72× shrink. The box then falls back to the node extents. Every other attribute in read.ts treats `""` as unset (Graphviz's default), so `bb=""` should give the inch unit too.
triage.cause: empty-string attribute not treated as unset

claim: DOT reader drops the color invis with a warning instead of reading it as transparent

triage.scenario: `a [color=invis]`, or a cluster with `pencolor=invis`. Graphviz treats `invis` like `transparent` and `none`. `dotColor` maps only `none` to `transparent`. `invis` goes to `x11Color`, comes back unchanged as `invis`, fails `checkedColor`, and is dropped with "DOT colors a diagram cannot draw were dropped: invis". The node then draws with the theme's stroke instead of no stroke.
triage.cause: `invis` not mapped to transparent

claim: DOT grayN/greyN values differ from Graphviz by one for some N (gray50, gray90)

triage.scenario: `color=gray50`: the formula `Math.round(50 * 2.55)` = `Math.round(127.5)` = 128 gives `#808080`, but Graphviz's X11 table (rgb.txt) has gray50 = 127 (`#7f7f7f`). The same happens for gray90: the formula gives 230 (`#e6e6e6`) where the table has 229 (`#e5e5e5`). Other levels match (gray10 = 26, gray30 = 77, gray70 = 179), so a rounding formula cannot reproduce the table. The file header says `x11.ts` comes from rgb.txt; the gray ramp should come from it too, as a table.
triage.cause: formula in place of rgb.txt table

claim: Cross-page connectors keep waypoints in the source scene's world, but import places pages in a different world, so the waypoints land in the wrong place

triage.scenario: a scene whose page run uses a non-default page layout (pages stacked vertically, or another gap) has a connector from a pasteboard shape to a shape on another page; it is exported to `crossPageEdges` with waypoints and label point in that scene's world coordinates, while its ends are exported page-relative. `documentSpecs` places the pages with `layoutPages(pageList)` (the default layout, since the document carries none) and adds the cross-page edge unshifted, so its bends and label land away from the ends they joined
triage.cause: world coordinates tied to a page placement the document does not record

claim: A connector to a container on the written page that leaves for another page is dropped from graph export with no warning

triage.scenario: a document whose `crossPageEdges` holds an edge from container `k` (on the page being written) to a node on page 2 → the "holds one page; connectors to other pages were dropped" check tests `byId` (nodes only), so it is false, and the edge is never written either; the writer reports nothing.
